title: Austria working on Carney Chukwuemeka allegiance switch before World Cup
content:
The Austrian Football Association are working on an agreement for Carney Chukwuemeka to switch his international allegiance ahead of the 2026 World Cup.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder has been capped up to under-20 level with England and was part of the under-19 side that won the 2022 European Championship.

The 22-year-old has not appeared for England’s senior side, however, and can switch his allegiance.

The former Chelsea and Aston Villa player was born in Eisenstadt, Austria, to Nigerian parents. He spent his early years in the country before moving to Northampton, England, and becoming a British citizen.

Chukwuemeka — who is also eligible to play for France — renounced his Austrian citizenship as part of that process, but is able to have it reinstated, as the decision was made for him when he was a minor.

The central midfielder, who joined Dortmund from Chelsea last summer after a successful loan spell, has scored three goals in 26 appearances in all competitions this season, starting six Bundesliga games.

Austria, coached by former Manchester United interim head coach Ralf Rangnick, qualified for the 2026 World Cup by finishing first in Group H, ahead of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Romania.

Austria start their World Cup group against Jordan at Levi’s Stadium, California, on June 16, ahead of games against Algeria and Argentina.
